messages:
Ria M (Sales): FYI customer (FinServ) SIG reviewer asked for detailed answers on encryption: at-rest + in-transit, custody options (BYOK/HSM), rotation cadence, and proof we can't access plaintext keys. They also want a CAIQ-friendly paragraph and POC steps. Can we draft something today?
Jordan P (Solutions): Yep. Two customer-facing flows: 1) Hosted API with Redwood-managed keys; 2) Private/Dedicated where customer provides KMS/HSM. Short draft incoming.
Anya K (Security): Drafting now. TL;DR: TLS1.3 for transit, AES-256-GCM at rest, keys stored in HSM/cloud KMS, plaintext not exportable, rotation supported, full audit logs. I'll paste a CAIQ-style block below you can copy into the questionnaire.
Anya K (Security): ```
CAIQ/Encryption response (suggested):
- Encryption in transit: All network traffic between clients and Redwood uses TLS 1.3 with AEAD ciphers (forward secrecy enabled).
- Encryption at rest: Customer data and model artifacts are encrypted using AES-256-GCM.
- Key custody: Keys are stored and used in hardware-backed key stores (HSM) or cloud KMS (CMEK/EKM) per customer configuration. For Hosted customers Redwood manages encryption keys by default; Enterprise customers may supply keys via supported BYOK integrations (KMIP, cloud KMS references) or deploy Redwood Private with customer-managed HSMs. Plaintext key material is never exported from a customer HSM and is never revealed to Redwood staff.
- Key rotation: Support for scheduled and on-demand rotation with key versioning; default rotation cadence is 90 days but is configurable based on customer policy. Rotation is performed by rewrapping key-encryption-keys; re-encryption workflows available for data if required.
- Access controls & audit: Key operations are governed by RBAC and dual-control where required. All KMS/HSM operations are logged; audit trails are retained per contractual retention.
- Attestation & compliance: For on-prem HSMs we can provide attestation artifacts; for cloud KMS we reference provider attestations (FIPS, SOC).
```
Jordan P (Solutions): Add link to POC playbook: https://redwood.internal/sales/poc/key-custody-playbook — includes sample KMIP config and minimal IAM perms.
Ria M (Sales): Customer also asked whether we can provide HSM attestation and sign contract language that we do not hold plaintext keys. Any suggested contract wording?
Anya K (Security): Suggested clause for legal: "Redwood shall not access, export, or persist Customer Master Keys in plaintext. Cryptographic operations shall be performed within Customer-controlled KMS/HSM or under customer-supplied key material; Redwood will only receive key references or wrapped keys and will not retain plaintext key material." Legal will want to iterate but this covers the ask.
Jordan P (Solutions): Sample single-line answer for SIG Q: 'Do you support customer-managed keys?' -> 'Yes. Customer-managed keys are supported in Private and Dedicated deployments via KMIP/CMEK/EKM integrations; in Hosted we also support BYOK via KMS key references. Plaintext keys are never exported to Redwood.'
Devon L (Eng): POC checklist (tech): 1) Provide test KMS/HSM endpoint or cloud project + service account with create/list/unwrap permissions; 2) network allowlist for control-plane endpoint (if Private); 3) sample wrapped key or KMS key ARN; 4) test dataset + consent for re-wrap verification. I can run the POC once we have creds.
Ria M (Sales): Important: customer asked about key destruction proof and backup handling.
Anya K (Security): We can state: 'Key destruction is performed per customer instruction; for HSMs we can provide deletion logs and attestation where supported. Backups use wrapped keys; key material backups are kept encrypted and tied to KMS protections. We can provide procedural documentation under NDA.'
Ria M (Sales): OK I'm going to assemble these answers and the CAIQ block and send to the SIG reviewer. If they accept POC, I'll ping Devon for next steps. Thanks all :thumbsup:
kms-bot: Reminder: refer to internal artifact store for HSM attestation templates: https://redwood.internal/artifacts/hsm-attestation-templates
Jordan P (Solutions): One more note — for Hosted customers who need cryptographic separation we can discuss tokenization or envelope encryption to minimize exposure.
Ria M (Sales): Great, sending now. Will update thread with responses.
